name: Walled Old Town (Rua Direita)
tagline: The storybook heart inside the ramparts
description: The whitewashed core along cobbled Rua Direita, running from Porta da Vila to the castle. Flower-draped houses, ginjinha doorways, shops, and restaurants line the way. Magical at dawn and dusk, packed with day-trippers midday. A romantic, characterful base for anyone wanting to live inside the postcard.
vibe: Historic, charming, touristy by day and hushed by night
bestFor: Slow travellers and couples who want heritage on their doorstep
pros: Unbeatable medieval atmosphere and rampart access
Walk to cafes, restaurants, and shops in minutes
Beautifully quiet once the coaches leave
cons: Heavy midday crowds and a tourist price premium
Cobbles, steps, and scarce long-term rentals

name: Castle End (The Pousada)
description: The town's highest point, where the medieval castle now runs as a pousada hotel. The lanes here are the quietest and most atmospheric, with the best views over the plain and walls. More about staying in style than settling in, but a serene, elevated corner of the old town.
bestFor: Short romantic stays and history lovers seeking calm
pros: Panoramic views and the most peaceful streets
Steps from the castle and rampart walk
cons: Limited dining and services right at the top
Steep cobbled approach and premium pricing

name: Below the Walls (Aqueduct and Porta da Vila)
tagline: Practical living at the town's threshold
description: The gentler flatter area just outside and below the ramparts, near the old aqueduct and the main Porta da Vila entrance. Parking, bus stops, and everyday services cluster here, with easier access than the stepped centre. A sensible, slightly better-value base still moments from the walled town.
bestFor: Longer-stay nomads who value access and parking
pros: Flat, easy access with parking and bus stops
Better-value rentals than inside the walls
Walk into the old town within minutes
cons: Less of the storybook atmosphere up top
Still passes through busy tourist entry points

name: Caldas da Rainha
tagline: The larger services town next door
description: A proper working town about ten minutes north, with a train station, hospital, markets, roomier cafes, and far more long-term rentals. Home to the daily fruit market and a spa heritage. Less pretty than Obidos but far more practical, and close to the Lagoa de Obidos and Foz do Arelho beaches.
bestFor: Nomads wanting value, amenities, and month-long rentals
pros: Broad services, markets, and cafe choice
Rail links and quick access to coast and lagoon
cons: You need transport to reach Obidos daily
